title: File Organization, RAID Storage & Advanced Indexing
subtitle: Heap/Sequential/Hash Files, RAID 0/1/5/6/10, Bitmap Indexing & Inverted Indexes
mentalModel: Storage architectures bridge the gap between volatile CPU memory and persistent physical disk blocks. RAID provides fault-tolerant block virtualization, while specialized indexing (Bitmap, Inverted, B+ Trees) optimizes I/O block transfers.

failureModes: RAID 5 Double Disk Crash: RAID 5 tolerates only 1 disk failure. A second disk failure during rebuild causes catastrophic array data loss.
Bitmap Index write locking: Updating a single row in a column with Bitmap indexes locks the entire bit vector, making Bitmap indexes unsuitable for high-concurrency OLTP.
Inverted Index postings list bloat: Frequent words (stop words) create giant postings lists that degrade search intersection performance without compression (e.g., Roaring Bitmaps).

tradeOffs.optionA: RAID 5: Higher usable storage capacity ((N-1)/N), but suffers write penalty (2 reads + 2 writes per modification).
tradeOffs.optionB: RAID 10: 50% capacity overhead, but delivers maximum random IOPS and faster rebuild times.

tradeOffs.aspect: B+ Tree Index vs Bitmap Index
tradeOffs.optionA: B+ Tree: High-cardinality unique columns (Primary Keys, IDs, Timestamps) with high write concurrency.
tradeOffs.optionB: Bitmap: Low-cardinality read-heavy analytical columns (Gender, Country, Status) in OLAP warehouses.

theoryData.productionScenario: An analytics query on 100,000,000 retail transactions filtering by Gender='F' AND Region='West' took 38 seconds on a standard B+ Tree index. Replacing it with an in-memory Bitmap Index reduced query runtime to 18 milliseconds by evaluating bitwise AND directly in CPU vector registers.

interviewQA.question: How does RAID 5 reconstruct lost data when a single disk fails?
interviewQA.answer: RAID 5 calculates parity P across data blocks using XOR: P = B1 ⊕ B2 ⊕ B3. When Disk 2 fails, its block B2 is reconstructed by XORing the surviving data blocks with the parity block: B2 = B1 ⊕ B3 ⊕ P.

interviewQA.question: What is an Inverted Index and where is it used?
interviewQA.answer: An Inverted Index is a data structure mapping words/tokens to the list of documents and positions where they occur. It is the core storage foundation of search engines (Elasticsearch, Apache Lucene) and full-text database extensions.

quizData.question: How many disk failures can a RAID 5 array tolerate without data loss?
quizData.explanation: RAID 5 uses single distributed parity (P), tolerating exactly 1 disk failure.

quizData.question: Which index type is best suited for low-cardinality attributes in read-heavy OLAP systems?
quizData.explanation: Bitmap Indexes represent low-cardinality distinct values with compact bit vectors that can be combined in CPU registers.
